crash_timing.crash_injection: fixture self-exits with status 137 after owner_crash_armed; no external kill tool is in the measurement clock
crash_timing.separate_overhead: fault_signal_to_death_ms records control-signal-to-death time and is excluded from takeover and useful-progress delays
crash_timing.takeover_clock: confirmed non-zero crash-fixture exit to new-owner takeover

protocol.pilot: three samples per TTL; settings frozen before final run
protocol.progress_boundary: timeout of the claimed affected attempt commits a replacement attempt

conclusions.takeover_and_progress: Observed per-episode takeover and first useful affected-work progress: owner_crash/100ms takeover 68.0 ms [9.4, 77.4], useful progress 194.0 ms [161.0, 212.3]; owner_pause/100ms takeover 85.9 ms [74.6, 92.4], useful progress 209.2 ms [180.9, 226.5]; owner_crash/250ms takeover 165.9 ms [153.2, 197.5], useful progress 457.7 ms [444.5, 474.8]; owner_pause/250ms takeover 242.9 ms [221.5, 248.8], useful progress 539.5 ms [504.7, 558.1]; owner_crash/750ms takeover 502.5 ms [497.0, 512.8], useful progress 1296.2 ms [1292.8, 1332.5]; owner_pause/750ms takeover 739.9 ms [717.7, 761.8], useful progress 1536.0 ms [1505.6, 1555.2]. Crash takeover and useful-progress clocks start at confirmed fixture death; signal-to-death overhead is reported separately.
conclusions.fault_comparison: Both owner-crash self-exit and owner-pause/resume episodes reached a new-owner replacement transition; comparisons remain bounded to this six-configuration local matrix.
conclusions.renewal_traffic: Renewal intervals are recorded as TTL/3: 60 stale-owner-safe episodes included 60 renewals before injection and 178 while the new owner waited for affected work.
conclusions.safety: Safety control passed: 0 false takeovers, 60 useful recoveries for 60 takeovers, and 180 stale-owner writes rejected.
conclusions.lock_contention: Measured 60 PostgreSQL lock-contention cases across the matrix with 0.6194 cumulative lock-wait seconds.
conclusions.pause_and_crash_limit: The crash fixture is a killed local process tree and the pause fixture is an in-process renewal pause; neither establishes host failure, storage durability, multi-host behavior, or production throughput.

limitations: owner crash and pause are bounded local process fixtures, not host or storage failure claims
the harness measures lease recovery mechanics, not production throughput or multi-host scale
short TTLs are measurement settings, not deployment recommendations
